flow: Part 2 个人陈述(准备1分钟,陈述1分30秒)+ 两人讨论(3分钟)

cue.t: Should college students be required to take part in volunteer work?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Many young people now prefer to work in big cities, while others choose to go back to their hometowns. Discuss with your partner the advantages and disadvantages of both choices.
task: Try to come to a conclusion.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
What do you usually do to relax after a busy week?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Please begin.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
I think big cities offer more job opportunities and higher salaries. That's why I want to stay in a big city.

steps.cue: 回应对方,并指出大城市的缺点

steps.t: Well, that's a problem. But small towns often don't have the jobs we studied for.

steps.cue: 承认对方的观点,补充回家乡的优点

steps.t: So maybe it depends on the person's career and priorities?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. Do you think the government should do more to help young people find jobs? Why?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: What do you usually do to relax after a busy week?
q1.ja: 忙碌的一周后,你通常怎么放松?
model: I usually go for a long walk in the park or watch a movie with my roommates. It helps me clear my mind and get ready for the next week.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Should college students be required to take part in volunteer work?
model: In my opinion, volunteer work should be encouraged, but it shouldn't be required. On the one hand, volunteering has many benefits. Students can develop a sense of responsibility and learn skills that they can't learn in the classroom. For example, last year I taught English to children in a rural school for two weeks, and it made me much more patient. On the other hand, if volunteering becomes compulsory, some students may do it only to get credits, without real enthusiasm. That would not help the people they are supposed to serve. So I think universities should offer more opportunities and rewards, but leave the final choice to students.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: Do you think the government should do more to help young people find jobs? Why?
q3.ja: 你认为政府应该做更多来帮助年轻人就业吗?为什么?
model: Yes, I do. The government could provide more training programs and support for small businesses, which create a lot of jobs. It could also help graduates in rural areas get internships. These measures would reduce unemployment and make society more stable.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: I think big cities offer more job opportunities and higher salaries. That's why I want to stay in a big city.
d1.ja: 回应对方,并指出大城市的缺点
model: That's true, but the cost of living in big cities is very high. Housing alone can take half of a young person's salary.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: Well, that's a problem. But small towns often don't have the jobs we studied for.
d2.ja: 承认对方的观点,补充回家乡的优点
model: I agree that's a challenge. However, with remote work, more jobs can be done from anywhere. And in your hometown, you can stay close to your family.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So maybe it depends on the person's career and priorities?
model: Exactly. It depends on the industry and what people value most. Young people should think carefully about their long-term goals before deciding.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

cue.t: Is artificial intelligence a help or a threat to college students?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Some people think university students should live on campus, while others prefer to rent an apartment off campus. Discuss the pros and cons with your partner.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
How often do you use social media, and what do you use it for?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Please begin.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
Living on campus is cheaper and more convenient. You can walk to class in five minutes.

steps.cue: 回应,并提出校外住宿的优点

steps.t: True, but living off campus can make you feel isolated from campus life.
So which do you think is better for first-year students?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. How do you think universities can better prepare students for their future careers?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: How often do you use social media, and what do you use it for?
q1.ja: 你多久用一次社交媒体?用来做什么?
model: I use it every day, mainly to keep in touch with my friends and to follow news about technology. I try to limit it to about an hour a day.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Is artificial intelligence a help or a threat to college students?
model: I believe artificial intelligence is mainly a help to college students, as long as we use it wisely. Today, many students use AI tools to search for information, check their grammar or get explanations of difficult concepts. For instance, when I didn't understand a statistics problem, an AI tool explained it to me step by step, which saved me a lot of time. However, there are also risks. Some students simply copy answers from AI and stop thinking for themselves, and the information AI gives is not always correct. Therefore, students should use AI as a learning partner, not as a replacement for their own work, and always check important facts.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: How do you think universities can better prepare students for their future careers?
q3.ja: 你认为大学怎样才能更好地帮助学生为将来的职业做准备?
model: Universities could offer more internships and invite professionals to share their experience. They could also teach practical skills like teamwork and communication, not just theory. This would help students move smoothly from campus to the workplace.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: Living on campus is cheaper and more convenient. You can walk to class in five minutes.
d1.ja: 回应,并提出校外住宿的优点
model: That's a good point. But living off campus gives you more privacy and freedom. In a dorm, it's hard to study when your roommates are noisy.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: True, but living off campus can make you feel isolated from campus life.
model: I agree. Campus activities are an important part of college. Maybe students who live off campus need to make more effort to join clubs.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So which do you think is better for first-year students?
model: For first-year students, I think living on campus is better, because it helps them make friends and adapt to college life. Later, they can choose for themselves.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

cue.t: Should people buy fewer things to protect the environment?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Some people think it is better to work for a large company, while others prefer a small company or a start-up. Discuss the pros and cons with your partner.
task: Try to come to a conclusion.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
What kind of books do you like to read, and why?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Please begin.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
I'd rather work for a large company. The salary is usually higher, and the job is more stable.

steps.cue: 回应对方,并指出小公司的优点

steps.t: But small companies can be risky. Some of them close after a few years.

steps.cue: 承认风险,并补充自己的看法

steps.t: So maybe it depends on what stage of your career you're at?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. How can young people find a balance between work and personal life?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: What kind of books do you like to read, and why?
q1.ja: 你喜欢读什么样的书?为什么?
model: I like reading biographies, because I can learn from the experiences of successful people and how they dealt with difficulties.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Should people buy fewer things to protect the environment?
model: In my opinion, people should buy fewer things, especially things they don't really need. First, producing goods uses a lot of energy and natural resources, and it creates pollution. Second, many products are thrown away after being used only a few times, which creates a huge amount of waste. For example, many of my classmates buy new clothes during online shopping festivals, but they only wear them once or twice. If we think carefully before buying, we can save money and reduce waste at the same time. In conclusion, buying less is a simple but effective way for everyone to protect the environment.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: How can young people find a balance between work and personal life?
q3.ja: 年轻人怎样才能在工作和个人生活之间取得平衡?
model: They should set clear boundaries, for example by not checking work messages late at night. It's also important to make time for exercise and friends, because a healthy life helps them work better.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: I'd rather work for a large company. The salary is usually higher, and the job is more stable.
d1.ja: 回应对方,并指出小公司的优点
model: That's true, but in a small company you can take on more responsibility and learn many different skills quickly.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: But small companies can be risky. Some of them close after a few years.
d2.ja: 承认风险,并补充自己的看法
model: I agree that's a risk. Still, the experience you gain there can be very valuable, even if the company doesn't last.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So maybe it depends on what stage of your career you're at?
model: Exactly. Young graduates might learn more at a start-up, while people who want stability may prefer a large company.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

cue.t: Is it necessary for college students to learn a second foreign language?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Many students now study in libraries, while others prefer studying in coffee shops. Discuss with your partner which place is better for studying.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
Who do you usually turn to when you have a problem? Why?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Please begin.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
I prefer coffee shops. The atmosphere is relaxing, and I can get a drink whenever I want.

steps.cue: 回应,并说明图书馆的优点

steps.t: True, but sometimes libraries are too quiet. I feel sleepy there.

steps.cue: 承认对方的观点,并补充

steps.t: So which do you think is better in the end?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying abroad?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: Who do you usually turn to when you have a problem? Why?
q1.ja: 遇到问题时,你通常向谁求助?为什么?
model: I usually talk to my older sister, because she has had similar experiences and always gives me honest advice.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Is it necessary for college students to learn a second foreign language?
model: I believe it's very useful, though not necessary for everyone. On the one hand, a second foreign language can open more doors in the job market, especially in international companies. It also helps us understand other cultures more deeply. For example, my roommate learned Spanish in her free time, and she got an internship at a company that trades with Latin America. On the other hand, learning a new language takes a lot of time, and some students are already very busy with their major courses. So in my view, students who are interested should be encouraged, but it shouldn't be required.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying abroad?
q3.ja: 出国留学有哪些优点和缺点?
model: Studying abroad helps students improve their language skills and become more independent. However, it's expensive, and some students feel lonely or find it hard to adapt to a new culture at first.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: I prefer coffee shops. The atmosphere is relaxing, and I can get a drink whenever I want.
d1.ja: 回应,并说明图书馆的优点
model: I see why you like that. But libraries are much quieter, and they have all the books and resources we need for research.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: True, but sometimes libraries are too quiet. I feel sleepy there.
d2.ja: 承认对方的观点,并补充
model: That's interesting. Some background noise can actually help people concentrate. But coffee shops can be crowded and expensive if you go every day.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So which do you think is better in the end?
model: I think it depends on the task. For reading and research, the library is better, but for group discussions or light work, a coffee shop can be a good choice.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

cue.t: Should universities require students to take physical education classes every year?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Some people think online shopping will replace shopping in physical stores. Discuss this with your partner.
task: Try to come to a conclusion.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
What do you think is the most important quality of a good friend?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Please begin.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
I think physical stores will disappear soon. Online shopping is cheaper and much more convenient.

steps.cue: 回应对方,并说明实体店的优点

steps.t: But many stores are already closing because people shop online.

steps.cue: 承认事实,并补充自己的看法

steps.t: So maybe stores won't disappear, but they will change?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. How do you think technology will change the way people work in the future?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: What do you think is the most important quality of a good friend?
q1.ja: 你认为好朋友最重要的品质是什么?
model: I think honesty is the most important quality. A good friend tells you the truth, even when it's not what you want to hear.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Should universities require students to take physical education classes every year?
model: In my opinion, universities should require physical education every year. First, many college students spend most of their day sitting in classrooms or in front of computers, so they don't get enough exercise. Second, regular exercise reduces stress and helps students concentrate on their studies. For example, when I was preparing for exams last term, playing badminton twice a week helped me sleep better and feel more positive. Some students may say they don't have time, but even one or two hours a week can make a big difference. Therefore, I believe PE classes are a good investment in students' health.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: How do you think technology will change the way people work in the future?
q3.ja: 你认为科技将如何改变人们未来的工作方式?
model: I think more people will work remotely, and AI will take over many repetitive tasks. So workers will need to keep learning new skills, especially creative and communication skills.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: I think physical stores will disappear soon. Online shopping is cheaper and much more convenient.
d1.ja: 回应对方,并说明实体店的优点
model: It's true that online shopping is convenient, but in a store you can try things on and get help from staff right away.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: But many stores are already closing because people shop online.
d2.ja: 承认事实,并补充自己的看法
model: That's right. However, some stores are changing. They offer experiences, like cafés or workshops, that you can't get online.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So maybe stores won't disappear, but they will change?
model: Exactly. Online and physical shopping will probably exist together, and successful stores will focus on giving customers a good experience.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去
